ui.note: baselineBytes: the ui page-load graph (dist/ui/index.js and its static imports, esbuild-minified, gzip -9) at 6ade3a0, before the in-chat media work. marginBytes: what the core media work may add: story 0 (media kinds, IRI and @id reading, page_open reports) +1.9 KB, story 1 (pictures, figure cards, safe URLs) +1.6 KB, story 2 (detection, the access gate, play buttons in both views, the first tap, the latest-episode fetch) +3.2 KB. The player itself is the lazy media chunk, not counted here. Then +3.0 KB for a remote agent's answer drawn as cards (the handoff `answer` part read and tidied, the cited cards, compact rows, and the link check for replies). Then +0.25 KB for 👍 and 👎 on a remote answer: the controller's feedback send, the answer's task, and the loader. The controls themselves (their DOM, styles and state) are a lazy chunk, loaded with the first answer that has an answerId. Then +0.5 KB for the header's window / full-screen toggle (its button, two icons, labels, styles, the stored choice and the nxis-mode-change event). Then +213 B for the guardrails: the loader and its fail-closed check, the hooks every turn passes through (input, the provider wrapper, the tool stage, the bound approval, the guarded run, a card's navigation), untrusted text kept apart as `data`, and the element's `guardrails` property with `lockdown`. With the 87 B that was left, that is the story's 300 B. The rules themselves are the lazy guardrails chunk, not counted here. Then +53 B so a second copy of the harness on a page (two versions, or the CDN build beside a bundled one) loads without throwing: @a2ui/lit defines its elements unguarded as it evaluates, so src/a2ui/define-once.ts skips a name already defined around that import, and define-restore.ts puts the registry's own define back. Then +431 B for `contained`: the window and its launcher drawn in the host's box as a preview, its property, the CSS that positions them against the box, what it turns off (discovery, preloading and loading the on-device model, stored conversations, resumed actions, and taking focus on connect), and its input off by default (the disabled composer, its placeholder, inert chips, and `allow-input` to turn it back on). Then +86 B for opening and closing from the page: `close()`, `isOpen`, and the `nxis-agent-toggle` event on every change. Then +1,942 B for event cards: the renderer spec's `happening` block, the answer view's hooks for events (the views and the tap, a lone event, rows, and the pick), loading the event cards' chunk and handing it the element's links, reports and form start, the calendar address from discovery, the handoff link's report token, and keeping the conversation when a handoff arrives from this chat. The cards themselves are the lazy `events` chunk, not counted here. Then +1,687 B for search forms as reads and the records first: a `method="get"` form's read-only test, its results URL and the visit that keeps the conversation, page titles in place of paths, form nouns in place of form ids, `when`, `from` and `to` on nxis_query with today's date, and the descriptions and instructions that put the site's records before a page's form. Reading a time and filtering records by it is a lazy chunk (`when`), not counted here. Then +2,240 B for one tool per form: grouping a site's forms by their endpoint, `nxis:fixedInput` read and used as the chooser, choices named by page title or the code in words, the merged schema's widened limits, checking a call against the chosen form's own fields with its tiers and limits in the refusal, sending only those fields, the card's "Get passes for", and the registry suffix dropped from every name a visitor reads. Then +38 B so a dated search that finds nothing never ends on "No results found.": the answer view reads the result's `notice` and says it, before the next events or in their place. Searching again from now on and wording the time is in the lazy `when` chunk, not counted here. Then +890 B so a turn never ends on result cards alone: after a read the model is asked again, to read on or answer in words (the answer step, its three bounds, the one nudge and its fallback lines, a read confirmed or completed later carried on to its answer and dropped when a newer turn starts, and the type listing's wording). Then +64 B so Chrome's native tools reach a model proxy with their names: the handoff tools built rather than spread, and a tool with no name left out of the request with a warning instead of sending one the model API refuses. Then +128 B so a tool runs on Chrome 158, whose executeTool takes only the Tool object getTools() returned: when the registry refuses the tool given (a copy, such as a handoff tool built for the turn, a stand-in, or none), the registry's own object for that name is read and called before falling back to the name.

media.note: The ./media chunk (src/media/*, loaded by a dynamic import() on the first Play tap) with whatever it alone pulls in, gzip -9.

guardrails.note: The ./guardrails chunk (src/guardrails/*, loaded by a dynamic import() at the first open or send, and awaited by every turn) with whatever it alone pulls in, gzip -9. Raised from 8192 to 8213 (+21 B) for a system prompt the model proxy holds (remote guardrails, part 4): the policy hook on the configuration and dropping the page's prompt for a remote model. Raised from 8213 to 8447 (+234 B) for the model proxy's policy (remote guardrails, part 5): loading the policy chunk when the element has guardrails-src, the version sent and checked on each completion, and a proxy's typed refusal said with the page's own message and reported as an nxis-guardrail event. Raised from 8447 to 8560 (+113 B) for kill switch messages that say which scope is off: the whole agent, or only its actions. Raised from 8560 to 8640 (+80 B) for copying each tool field by field when its description is wrapped, since Chrome's native tools keep their fields on the prototype and a spread dropped them, name and schema included.

guardrailsRemote.note: The chunk that fetches the model proxy's guardrails policy (src/guardrails/remote.ts and policy-core.ts, loaded by a dynamic import() from the guardrails only when the element has guardrails-src), gzip -9. It shares the guardrails' settingsFor and glob rather than splitting them into a chunk of their own, which would cost the guardrails chunk about 600 B in lost compression.

events.note: The event cards' chunk (src/ui/event-cards.ts, with the event model src/harness/happening.ts and the A2UI surfaces src/a2ui/events.ts, loaded by a dynamic import() with the first result that is an event) with whatever it alone pulls in, gzip -9. About 8.3 KB at its introduction.

lazyChunk.note: Every lazy chunk of the ui entry without a budget of its own (today the sources panel, about 3.2 KB, and the feedback controls, about 2.5 KB, each loaded by a dynamic import() on first use), with whatever it alone pulls in, gzip -9.

cdnProxy.note: The CDN build's proxy.js (createProxyProvider, self-contained), which a page imports beside ui.js to point the element at a model proxy, gzip -9. Built apart from ui.js so ui.js stays exactly the ./ui bundle measured above.
